title: Beef Stroganoff
subtitle: Tender beef strips in a creamy paprika and mustard sauce
excerpt: Thinly sliced beef sirloin cooked quickly in butter with mushrooms and onion, then finished in a soured cream sauce with paprika and Worcestershire sauce. It comes together in about 25 minutes and is best served over egg noodles or with rice.
sourceNotes: Based on the classic Russian dish beef Stroganov, widely popularised in British and American home cooking from the mid-20th century.

content.text: The beef must be sliced thinly, no more than 5mm, and cooked very quickly over high heat. If the pan is crowded or the heat too low, the beef steams and turns grey instead of browning. Cook in two batches if your pan is not large enough.

items.prepNote: sliced thinly across the grain, about 5mm

content.text: Heat half the butter in a large frying pan over a high heat until foaming. Season the beef slices with salt and pepper. Fry in a single layer for 1 to 2 minutes per side until browned. Remove and set aside. Do this in batches if needed.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the remaining butter, then the onion. Cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes until the mushrooms are golden.
Stir in the paprika, mustard, and Worcestershire sauce. Cook for 1 minute.

Remove the pan from the heat and stir in the soured cream. Return the beef and any resting juices to the pan and stir gently. Heat over a low heat for 1 to 2 minutes, but do not let it boil or the cream may split.
Scatter with parsley and serve over egg noodles or rice.

items.cause: Sauce boiled after cream was added
items.fix: Keep heat very low after adding cream; do not let it bubble.

items.cause: Pan overcrowded or heat too low
items.fix: Cook in batches over high heat for 1 minute each side.
